item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Channel members can post messages shown as a webhook via client-supplied message metadata
item.description:
CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N) · CWE-290, CWE-345, CWE-863
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.7.0, < 0.12.2 (patched: 0.12.2)
---
# Channel members can post messages shown as a webhook via client-supplied message metadata
## Summary Any member who can post in a channel can make their message appear as if a real webhook of that channel posted it. The server stored the metadata the client sent with a message without checking it. The channel then showed the message under the webhook's name and role, with no webhook token required.
## Preconditions Channels are enabled (`ENABLE_CHANNELS`, default `False`). The channel has at least one webhook. The attacker is a member with write access to the channel. The attacker knows the webhook's id. Any member can read it from a message the webhook posted, so it is not a secret. Instances with channels disabled, or without channel webhooks, are not affected.
## Impact A member can post, edit and pin messages that other members see as coming from a trusted webhook, such as an alerting or ops bot. That makes social engineering inside the channel easy. The stored author is still the attacker's account. The attacker cannot change the webhook's real messages, read anything new or act with the webhook's token.
## Fix Fixed in #32421. The server now drops any message metadata sent by the client, both when a message is posted and when it is edited, so only the server sets it. Upgrading is enough.
## Root cause Component: the channel message post and edit endpoints in `backend/open_webui/routers/channels.py`. Affected setup: every build with channel webhooks, from 0.7.0. The message form accepted an arbitrary metadata object from the client and stored it as is. The message list and the pinned list then trusted that metadata to decide who the message was from. A webhook id in the metadata was enough for the message to be shown as that webhook.
## Proof of concept 1. Admin creates a webhook "Ops Bot" in a channel, and the webhook posts a message. 2. Alice, a channel member, reads the webhook id from that message. 3. Alice posts a message with `meta.webhook = {"id": "<webhook id>", "name": "Ops Bot"}` and pins it. 4. Bob opens the channel. The message and the pinned list show it as `Ops Bot` with role `webhook`, while the stored author is Alice.
Run by the reporter on 0.11.3.
## Credits @Tarekinh0 (reporter)

item.title: [CRITICAL] go:github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2 — Argo CD: AppProject destination-namespace and resource restrictions bypassed by PreDelete/PostDelete resource hooks (CVE-2026-77459)
item.description:
CVE-2026-77459 · CVSS 9.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H) · CWE-863
Affected: - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2 >= 2.10.0, <= 2.14.21 - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.0.0, < 3.3.15 (patched: 3.3.15) - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.4.0, < 3.4.10 (patched: 3.4.10) - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.5.0, < 3.5.4 (patched: 3.5.4) - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.6.0-rc1, < 3.6.0-rc2 (patched: 3.6.0-rc2)
---
### Impact
Argo CD checks an Application's AppProject before it creates resources during a sync. That check covers destination namespaces and servers, cluster-scoped resource allow and deny lists, and namespaced resource allow and deny lists, including resource names. PreDelete and PostDelete hooks skip it. When the Application is deleted, Argo CD creates those hooks with the application-controller's credentials on the destination cluster.
All versions from v2.10.0 onward are affected, including every currently supported release. v2.9.22 and earlier are not. PostDelete hooks were introduced in [dcc17f70bf](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/dcc17f70bf7db973fe480b8b613189b2c5ac4b4b) (2023-12-18, [#16595](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/16595)) and first released in v2.10.0. That creation path has never applied the project check. PreDelete hooks, added in [3bf3d8a212](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/3bf3d8a2124e772ac651f3fd42375c4e9b8008af) (2025-12-05, [#22288](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/22288)) and first released in v3.3.0, use the same path. v3.2.12 and earlier do not have PreDelete hooks. PreSync, Sync, PostSync, and SyncFail hooks still go through the project check.
A user who can push to the Git repository an Application syncs from can commit a hook whose namespace, group, kind, or name the AppProject would refuse on sync. The controller adds the delete finalizer when it sees the hook, and the Application stays Synced until someone deletes it. Deleting the Application creates the hook. What that can reach is bounded by the application-controller's access to the destination cluster. In a typical install that access is broad, so a tenant can create a cluster-scoped object such as a `ClusterRoleBinding`, or an object in a namespace the project does not allow. A hook with no deletion policy is removed after it succeeds. A deletion policy that does not remove the hook on success leaves the object in the cluster. A hook such as a Job can create further objects that Argo CD does not clean up.
### Patches
A patch for this vulnerability has been released in the following Argo CD versions:
* v3.6.0-rc2 * v3.5.4 * v3.4.10 * v3.3.15
The fix applies the same AppProject destination and resource checks used on sync before creating a PreDelete or PostDelete hook.
Argo CD 2.x and 3.0 through 3.2 are out of support and will not receive a patch. Upgrade to a patched 3.3 or newer release.
### Workarounds
There is no configuration setting that applies the project check to delete hooks while those hooks stay in use.
* Do not grant untrusted users write access to Git repositories that back Applications in restrictive AppProjects. * Limit who can delete Applications. Deletion is what runs PreDelete and PostDelete hooks. * Tighten the application-controller's Kubernetes access so a hook cannot reach sensitive namespaces or APIs.
### Credits
The Argo CD team would like to thank @RealFakeAccount, @AdamKorcz, @0xshylines, @thevilledev, @HenriWilliams, @cherez0ff, @ARSB1, and @zwindler for responsibly disclosing this issue according to our [security reporting guidelines](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/master/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability).
### References
* PostDelete introducing commit: [dcc17f70bf7db973fe480b8b613189b2c5ac4b4b](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/dcc17f70bf7db973fe480b8b613189b2c5ac4b4b) ([#16595](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/16595)), first released in v2.10.0 * PreDelete introducing commit: [3bf3d8a2124e772ac651f3fd42375c4e9b8008af](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/3bf3d8a2124e772ac651f3fd42375c4e9b8008af) ([#22288](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/22288)), first released in v3.3.0 * [AppProject specification](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/projects/) * [Resource hooks](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/resource_hooks/)

item.title: [HIGH] espocrm/espocrm — Unauthenticated long body request loads CPU in the password-redaction regex, denying service
item.description:
CVSS 7.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H)
Affected: - php/EspoCRM <=10.0.7 (patched: 10.0.8)
---
## Summary
An unauthenticated attacker can send specially crafted API requests that trigger excessive CPU usage during error handling. By sending a small number of large requests concurrently, an attacker can exhaust available server workers, making EspoCRM slow or unavailable to legitimate users.

item.title: [HIGH] go:github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2 — Argo CD repo-server command injection via crafted SSH repository SOCKS5 proxy URL (CVE-2026-55797)
item.description:
CVE-2026-55797 · CVSS 8.8 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H) · CWE-78
Affected: - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2 >= 2.11.0, <= 2.14.21 - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.0.0, < 3.3.15 (patched: 3.3.15) - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.4.0, < 3.4.10 (patched: 3.4.10) - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.5.0, < 3.5.4 (patched: 3.5.4) - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 = 3.6.0-rc1 (patched: 3.6.0-rc2)
---
### Impact
Argo CD runs a shell command in the repo-server when it clones or fetches an SSH Git repository that has a proxy URL. The proxy host and port are copied into an SSH `ProxyCommand`. A host that contains shell metacharacters breaks out of that command and runs in the repo-server.
All versions from v2.11.0 onward are affected, including every currently supported release. v2.10.20 and earlier are not. The behavior was introduced in [9b27aeb1a4](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/9b27aeb1a4fb15d11a0f01cad65dea1fdfc60205) (2024-01-09, [#15864](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/15864)), the change that added SOCKS5 proxy support for SSH Git URLs, and was first released in v2.11.0.
The repository must use SSH. `http`, `https`, and `socks5` proxy URLs all take this path when they are set on an SSH repository. An HTTPS Git repository uses the proxy as an HTTP proxy and does not build this command.
Anyone who can create or update a repository or a repository credential template can set the proxy. That includes a project-scoped repository permission, `argocd repo add --proxy`, and a repository Secret. A credential template applies its proxy to every matching SSH repository that does not have its own credentials. Argo CD runs the command when it tests the repository connection and on later fetches. The process can read other Git, Helm, and OCI credentials stored for the repo-server.
### Patches
A patch for this vulnerability has been released in the following Argo CD versions:
* v3.6.0-rc2 * v3.5.4 * v3.4.10 * v3.3.15
The fix stops passing the proxy host and port through a shell.
Argo CD 2.x and 3.0 through 3.2 are out of support and will not receive a patch. Upgrade to a patched 3.3 or newer release.
### Workarounds
There is no setting that keeps SSH repository proxies and removes the shell command.
* Do not grant repository create or update to untrusted users, including project-scoped repository access. See [RBAC resources](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/rbac/#rbac-model-structure) and [project-scoped repositories](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/projects/#project-scoped-repositories-and-clusters). * Do not set a proxy on an SSH repository or on a credential template that matches SSH repositories. The proxy field is documented in [Configure repositories with proxy](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/declarative-setup/#configure-repositories-with-proxy). Credential templates are documented in [Credential templates](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/private-repositories/#credential-templates). The `--proxy` flag is documented in [`argocd repo add`](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/commands/argocd_repo_add/).
An HTTPS Git repository with an HTTP proxy does not use this command. Review existing repository and credential-template Secrets for unexpected `proxy` values.
### Credits
The Argo CD team would like to thank @kamil-sawicki, @yuvalelarat, @cherez0ff, @McCaulay, @gehan-psbc, @ria-labs-security, @parameter-ai-security, and @zwindler for responsibly disclosing this issue according to our [security reporting guidelines](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/master/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability).
### References
* Introducing commit: [9b27aeb1a4fb15d11a0f01cad65dea1fdfc60205](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/9b27aeb1a4fb15d11a0f01cad65dea1fdfc60205) ([#15864](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/15864)), first released in v2.11.0 * [Configure repositories with proxy](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/declarative-setup/#configure-repositories-with-proxy)
### For more information

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Local privilege escalation to root in DEB/RPM packages (packager.io) (CVE-2026-102490)
item.description:
CVE-2026-102490 · CVSS 8.5 (CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-250, CWE-426, CWE-732
Affected: - other/Zammad <= 7.2.1 (patched: 7.2.2)
---
Zammad packages built with packager.io (DEB and RPM) could have allowed a local attacker who already had code execution as the unprivileged `zammad` service account to escalate to full `root` privileges on the host. Service processes began running as `root` and executed files that were owned and writable by the `zammad` account before dropping to that account, and the installation directory was writable by it. An attacker holding that foothold could have escalated within seconds, because the affected services were restarted automatically whenever they stopped; no administrator interaction was required. Only installations from the DEB and RPM packages were affected — installations from source or the official container images were not. All released packaged versions were affected.
Credit: The Dutch Institute for Vulnerability Disclosure Foundation (DIVD)

item.title: [MEDIUM] argoproj/argo-cd — An oversized OCI manifest can exhaust repo-server memory
item.description:
CVSS 6.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H)
Affected: - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.1.0, < 3.3.15 || >= 3.4.0, < 3.4.10 || >= 3.5.0, < 3.5.4 || = 3.6.0-rc1 (patched: 3.3.15, 3.4.10, 3.5.4, 3.6.0-rc2)
---
### Impact
Argo CD reads an OCI image manifest into memory with no size limit. A registry can return a manifest large enough to exhaust the repo-server. Kubernetes then kills the process, and manifest generation stops for every Application until the pod restarts. The same request can be sent again after the restart.
All versions from v3.1.0 onward are affected, including every currently supported release. v3.0.23 and earlier are not. The behavior was introduced in [18c4d9d568](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/18c4d9d56869531f7ae017d610d4e79aaa5525c3) (2025-06-06, [#18646](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/18646)), the change that added OCI as an application source, and was first released in v3.1.0.
Argo CD downloads the manifest when it renders an Application whose source is an OCI registry, and when it loads that source's metadata. Resolving a tag to a digest does not download the manifest. The `--oci-manifest-max-extracted-size` flag (default 1G) limits the unpacked image archive. It does not limit the manifest document. See [argocd-repo-server](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/server-commands/argocd-repo-server/).
Someone who can make Argo CD pull from a registry they control can trigger this. That includes creating an Application with an `oci://` source, which the `default` project's `sourceRepos: ['*']` allows. See [OCI](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/oci/) and [the default project](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/projects/#the-default-project). A person who can push to a registry an Application already uses can do the same. This is the OCI counterpart of the Helm index limit in [GHSA-jhwx-mhww-rgc3](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/security/advisories/GHSA-jhwx-mhww-rgc3).
### Patches
A patch for this vulnerability has been released in the following Argo CD versions:
* v3.6.0-rc2 * v3.5.4 * v3.4.10 * v3.3.15
The fix rejects an OCI manifest larger than 4 MiB.
Argo CD 3.1 and 3.2 are affected and out of support. They will not receive a patch. Upgrade to a patched 3.3 or newer release.
### Workarounds
There is no setting that caps the OCI manifest document.
* Allow only registries you trust in the AppProject `sourceRepos` list. The `default` project allows every source until that list is changed. See [Projects](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/projects/). * Do not grant untrusted users permission to create Applications or repositories that point at other registries. See [RBAC resources](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/rbac/#rbac-model-structure).
A user who can push to a registry already listed in `sourceRepos` can still publish an oversized manifest.
### Credits
The Argo CD team would like to thank @andrejtomci for responsibly disclosing this issue according to our [security reporting guidelines](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/master/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability).
### References
* Introducing commit: [18c4d9d56869531f7ae017d610d4e79aaa5525c3](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/18c4d9d56869531f7ae017d610d4e79aaa5525c3) ([#18646](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/18646)), first released in v3.1.0 * [OCI](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/oci/) * [GHSA-jhwx-mhww-rgc3](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/security/advisories/GHSA-jhwx-mhww-rgc3), the Helm index size limit

item.title: [MEDIUM] argoproj/argo-cd — Extension proxy RBAC ignores application namespace when applications-in-any-namespace is enabled
item.description:
CVSS 4.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N) · CWE-284, CWE-863
Affected: - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2 >= 2.7.0 - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.0.0, < 3.3.15 || >= 3.4.0, < 3.4.10 || >= 3.5.0, < 3.5.4 || = 3.6.0-rc1 (patched: 3.3.15, 3.4.10, 3.5.4, 3.6.0-rc2)
---
### Impact
Argo CD's proxy extension checks Application `get` before it forwards a request to an extension backend. When applications in any namespace are enabled, that check uses the wrong application name. The namespace is left out, so the policy object is `project/name` instead of `project/namespace/name`. The Application API still uses the three-part name.
All versions from v2.7.0 onward are affected, including every currently supported release. v2.6.15 and earlier do not include this check. The behavior was introduced in [974c2de168](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/974c2de1686521437fa755a180b8d0593e9c0533) (2023-02-15, [#11694](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/11694)), the change that added authorization to proxy extensions, and was first released in v2.7.0.
Both features have to be turned on. Proxy extensions are off unless `server.enable.proxy.extension` is set. Applications in any namespace are off unless the API server and application controller are started with the extra application namespaces. An install that keeps every Application in the Argo CD namespace is not affected.
An authenticated user who can invoke a proxy extension, and who has Application `get` on `project/name` or on a wildcard such as `project/*`, can invoke that extension against an Application of the same name in another namespace of the same project. A deny rule written as `project/namespace/name` is not evaluated on this path. The Application API still returns a denial for that Application. The extension backend receives the request, the destination cluster name and URL, and the caller's identity.
### Patches
A patch for this vulnerability has been released in the following Argo CD versions:
* v3.6.0-rc2 * v3.5.4 * v3.4.10 * v3.3.15
The fix checks the extension request with the Argo CD namespace as the default, which is how the Application API builds the policy object.
Argo CD 2.x and 3.0 through 3.2 are out of support and will not receive a patch. Upgrade to a patched 3.3 or newer release.
### Workarounds
There is no setting that restores the three-part application check while proxy extensions and applications in any namespace both stay enabled.
* Leave proxy extensions disabled. They are off by default. To turn them off, do not set `server.enable.proxy.extension` to `true` in `argocd-cmd-params-cm`, and remove `extension.config` from `argocd-cm`. See [Proxy extension configuration](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/developer-guide/extensions/proxy-extensions/#configuration). * Do not enable [applications in any namespace](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/app-any-namespace/). With every Application in the Argo CD namespace, `project/name` is the policy object the rest of the API uses. Namespace-scoped rules are documented in [Application in any namespaces](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/rbac/#application-in-any-namespaces). * Limit who can invoke an extension. That does not fix the application check. See [The extensions resource](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/rbac/#the-extensions-resource).
### Credits
The Argo CD team would like to thank @komyunghan, @Nadav0077, @akshatgit, @rexpository, @LHeiakim, @edwardav970, @dhki, @arbor-s, and @ninthlife-tools for responsibly disclosing this issue according to our [security reporting guidelines](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/master/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability).
### References
* Introducing commit: [974c2de1686521437fa755a180b8d0593e9c0533](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/974c2de1686521437fa755a180b8d0593e9c0533) ([#11694](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/11694)), first released in v2.7.0 * [Applications in any namespace](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/app-any-namespace/) * [Proxy extensions](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/developer-guide/extensions/proxy-extensions/) * [Application in any namespaces](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/rbac/#application-in-any-namespaces)

item.title: [HIGH] argoproj/argo-cd — Login failure rate limit can be bypassed via concurrent requests (CVE-2025-61560)
item.description:
CVE-2025-61560 · CVSS 7.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N) · CWE-307, CWE-362
Affected: - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd >= 1.5.3, < 2.0.0 - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2 >= 2.0.0 - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.0.0, < 3.3.15 || >= 3.4.0, < 3.4.10 || >= 3.5.0, < 3.5.4 || = 3.6.0-rc1 (patched: 3.3.15, 3.4.10, 3.5.4, 3.6.0-rc2)
---
### Impact
Argo CD limits failed local username/password logins. The default is 5 failures in a 5-minute window, set by `ARGOCD_SESSION_FAILURE_MAX_FAIL_COUNT` and `ARGOCD_SESSION_FAILURE_WINDOW_SECONDS`. The limit applies to local accounts, including the built-in `admin` account when it is enabled. It does not apply to SSO or OIDC logins.
The login handler reads the failure count, checks the password, and only then increments the count. Concurrent requests for the same username all read the count before any of them updates it, so more guesses complete than the configured maximum. A correct password in that burst still returns a session token. Failed attempts in the burst return the same invalid-login response as an ordinary failure.
All versions from v1.5.3 onward are affected, including every currently supported release. v1.5.2 and earlier do not have this throttle. The behavior was introduced in [76bacfdea4](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/76bacfdea4d9bbce774887f18a62e3ebc27d486c) (2020-04-21, [#3404](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/3404)) and first released in v1.5.3.
Anyone who can reach `POST /api/v1/session` can attempt this. No Argo CD account is required. A separate cap, `ARGOCD_MAX_CONCURRENT_LOGIN_REQUESTS_COUNT` (default 50), limits how many login requests one API server process handles at once. It is not per username, so it does not make the failure count correct. Each API server process stores its own failure counts. A second replica enforces its own limit.
### Patches
A patch for this vulnerability has been released in the following Argo CD versions:
* v3.6.0-rc2 * v3.5.4 * v3.4.10 * v3.3.15
The fix handles one local login attempt per username at a time, so the failure count is updated before the next attempt is checked.
Argo CD 1.x, 2.x, and 3.0 through 3.2 are out of support and will not receive a patch. Upgrade to a patched 3.3 or newer release, or disable local accounts and use SSO.
### Workarounds
Disable local accounts and require SSO. That removes the password check this limit applies to.
* Disable the built-in `admin` account with `admin.enabled: "false"` in `argocd-cm`. See [Disable admin user](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/user-management/#disable-admin-user). * Disable any other local account with `accounts.<username>.enabled: "false"`. See [Local users/accounts](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/user-management/#local-usersaccounts). * Configure [SSO](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/user-management/#sso) for login.
Where a local account must stay enabled, set a strong unique password ([Manage users](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/user-management/#manage-users)). Lowering `ARGOCD_MAX_CONCURRENT_LOGIN_REQUESTS_COUNT` shrinks how many login attempts can be in flight on one API server process ([Failed logins rate limiting](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/user-management/#failed-logins-rate-limiting)). That cap is not per username, so it does not make the failure counter correct. With more than one API server replica, set `ARGOCD_API_SERVER_REPLICAS` so the cap is divided across them ([argocd-server](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/operator-manual/high_availability/#argocd-server)).
Restricting network access to the API, or putting an HTTP rate limit in front of it, reduces how many attempts can arrive. Those are not Argo CD settings, and the project docs do not describe them.
### Credits

item.title: [CRITICAL] argoproj/argo-cd — A Jsonnet import can read files from the repo-server
item.description:
CVSS 9.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Affected: - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd >= 0.9.0, < 2.0.0 - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2 >= 2.0.0 - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.0.0, < 3.3.15 || >= 3.4.0, < 3.4.10 || >= 3.5.0, < 3.5.4 || = 3.6.0-rc1 (patched: 3.3.15, 3.4.10, 3.5.4, 3.6.0-rc2)
---
### Impact
Argo CD evaluates `.jsonnet` files inside the repo-server with an importer that can open any path the process can read. `import`, `importstr`, and `importbin` all use that importer. An absolute path such as `/proc/self/environ`, a `../` traversal, or a symlink inside the repository that points outside it is opened with the repo-server’s own filesystem permissions. `importstr` of a device such as `/dev/zero` reads until the process runs out of memory. Argo CD redacts generated Secrets, so placing the file contents in a ConfigMap returns them to the caller. The data can include the process environment, the projected service-account token, mounted private keys, and repository credentials.
All versions from v0.9.0 onward are affected, including every currently supported release. v0.8.2 and earlier are not. The behavior was introduced in [27471d524](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/27471d524958878e7acc5131fb466b292079cd05) (2018-09-07, [#561](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/561)), the change that added Jsonnet as an application source, and was first released in v0.9.0. The import path was limited to a search list for relative paths. That list does not apply to absolute paths.
Two ways to supply the file:
* Commit a `.jsonnet` file to a Git repository that an Application builds. Directory applications evaluate every `.jsonnet` file in the application directory. * Upload it through `POST /api/v1/applications/manifestsWithFiles` (`argocd app diff --local --server-side-generate`). This needs only Application `get` on an existing directory Application. It does not need permission to update or sync the Application, or write access to its Git repository.
### Patches
A patch for this vulnerability has been released in the following Argo CD versions:
* v3.6.0-rc2 * v3.5.4 * v3.4.10 * v3.3.15
Imports that stay inside the repository still work. The patch resolves each import, including symlinks, and rejects any path outside the repository root. It also rejects anything that is not a regular file, so a device file is not read.
### Workarounds
Set `jsonnet.enable` to `"false"` in the [`argocd-cm` ConfigMap](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/tool_detection/#disable-built-in-tools). Argo CD then skips `.jsonnet` files. That covers a file committed to Git and a file uploaded through `POST /api/v1/applications/manifestsWithFiles`. YAML and JSON in a directory application are still applied. An application that depends on Jsonnet stops rendering those files: they are omitted rather than rejected, so a directory that contains only Jsonnet syncs without those manifests.
### Credits
The Argo CD team would like to thank @hoang-prod, @arpitjain099, @key-moon, @MopMonkAI, @Kushalkhemka, @PontusHanssen, @mayank-jangid-moon, @skigeek16, @opensec-intelligence, @thevilledev, @ShadowByte1, @izhax, @mikecole-mg, @jake-ciolek, and @vitorespf for responsibly disclosing this issue according to our [security reporting guidelines](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/master/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability).

item.title: [CRITICAL] argoproj/argo-cd — A Kustomize Helm config home can run commands in the repo-server
item.description:
CVSS 9.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Affected: - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2 >= 2.1.0 - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.0.0, < 3.3.15 || >= 3.4.0, < 3.4.10 || >= 3.5.0, < 3.5.4 || = 3.6.0-rc1 (patched: 3.3.15, 3.4.10, 3.5.4, 3.6.0-rc2)
---
### Impact
When Kustomize Helm chart rendering is enabled, a kustomization can point Helm at a directory the repository controls and run a program from that directory inside `argocd-repo-server`. Kustomize copies `helmGlobals.configHome` into Helm’s config and data directories. Helm then loads a downloader plugin from `<configHome>/.data/plugins` with no separate plugin-install step, and runs it when a `helmCharts` repository URL uses that plugin’s protocol. The command runs as the repo-server user and can read repository credentials and anything else available to that process.
All versions from v2.1.0 onward are affected, including every currently supported release. v2.0.5 and earlier are not. The behavior was introduced in [b6d5c23bc](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/b6d5c23bce2f8a46c52975ba438a3b93d242d96c) (2021-04-20, [#6059](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/6059)), the change that upgraded the bundled Kustomize from 3.9.4 to 4.1.2, and was first released in v2.1.0. Kustomize 4.1.0 is what first passes `helmGlobals.configHome` through to Helm ([kubernetes-sigs/kustomize#3784](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/3784)). Deployments that do not pass `--enable-helm` to `kustomize build` are not affected.
Two ways to supply the kustomization, both of which require that an operator has already enabled `--enable-helm`:
* Commit it to a Git repository that an Application builds with Kustomize. * Upload it through `POST /api/v1/applications/manifestsWithFiles` (`argocd app diff --local --server-side-generate`). This needs only Application `get` on an existing Application. It does not need permission to update or sync the Application, or write access to its Git repository.
### Patches
A patch for this vulnerability has been released in the following Argo CD versions:
* v3.6.0-rc2 * v3.5.4 * v3.4.10 * v3.3.15
Kustomize Helm chart rendering still works for ordinary `http`, `https`, and `oci` chart repositories. The patch points Helm at an empty config and data directory for every Kustomize build, so `helmGlobals.configHome` cannot register a plugin.
### Workarounds
Do not pass `--enable-helm` in [`kustomize.buildOptions`](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/kustomize/#kustomizing-helm-charts). That is a complete workaround for this issue. Applications that render Helm charts through Kustomize cannot use it.
Restricting Application `get`, or blocking `POST /api/v1/applications/manifestsWithFiles`, closes only the upload path. A kustomization committed to Git is still built on the next sync while `--enable-helm` is set.
### Credits
The Argo CD team would like to thank @hoang-prod for responsibly disclosing this issue according to our [security reporting guidelines](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/master/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability).
### References
* Introducing commit: [b6d5c23bce2f8a46c52975ba438a3b93d242d96c](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/b6d5c23bce2f8a46c52975ba438a3b93d242d96c) ([#6059](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/6059)), first released in v2.1.0 * Kustomize feature: [kubernetes-sigs/kustomize#3784](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kustomize/pull/3784) * [Kustomizing Helm charts](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/kustomize/#kustomizing-helm-charts)

item.title: [CRITICAL] argoproj/argo-cd — A Kustomize remote ref can run commands in the repo-server
item.description:
CVSS 9.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Affected: - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v2 >= 2.7.0 - go/github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/v3 >= 3.0.0, < 3.3.15 || >= 3.4.0, < 3.4.10 || >= 3.5.0, < 3.5.4 || = 3.6.0-rc1 (patched: 3.3.15, 3.4.10, 3.5.4, 3.6.0-rc2)
---
### Impact
Kustomize passes a remote resource, base, or component URL to `git fetch`, and appends that URL’s `ref` or `version` query value with no `--` separator. A value that starts with `-`, such as `--upload-pack=<command>`, is parsed as a Git option. `--upload-pack` runs that command inside `argocd-repo-server` when the remote is a local transport such as `file://`. Git does not run it for an `https://` remote. A `file://` URL never leaves the pod, and Git returns the command’s output to the caller in the manifest-generation error. The command runs as the repo-server user and can read repository credentials and anything else available to that process.
All versions from v2.7.0 onward are affected, including every currently supported release. v2.6.15 and earlier are not. The behavior was introduced in [25badeb7a1](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/25badeb7a1e154805340bb7237e0ce671f3772dd) (2023-03-16, [#12299](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/12299)), the change that upgraded the bundled Kustomize from 4.5.7 to 5.0.1, and was first released in v2.7.0. Kustomize 4.5.7 rejects a `file://` URL, so this payload does not run there. Kustomize 5.0.0 is what first accepts `file://` and hands it to `git fetch`. Replacing the repo-server binary with a newer Kustomize does not help: current Kustomize still passes `ref` through without `--`.
Two ways to supply the Kustomization:
* Commit it to a Git repository that an Application builds with Kustomize. * Upload it through `POST /api/v1/applications/manifestsWithFiles` (`argocd app diff --local --server-side-generate`). This needs only Application `get` on an existing Application. It does not need permission to update or sync the Application, or write access to its Git repository.
### Patches
A patch for this vulnerability has been released in the following Argo CD versions:
* v3.6.0-rc2 * v3.5.4 * v3.4.10 * v3.3.15
The patch keeps Kustomize remote bases working. It places a `git` wrapper ahead of the real `git` on the Kustomize build’s `PATH`, so the remote URL and `ref` cannot be parsed as Git options.
### Workarounds
Pin every Application that runs Kustomize to a Kustomize older than 5.0, such as 4.5.7. Register that binary with [`kustomize.path.<version>`](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/kustomize/#custom-kustomize-versions) in `argocd-cm`, and set `spec.source.kustomize.version` (or `argocd app set <app> --kustomize-version`) on each Application. The binary that actually runs has to be that older one. Leaving Kustomize 5.x as the default, or as another registered version, leaves that path open.
Applications that rely on Kustomize 5 features cannot use this pin. Those builds will fail or drop behavior that 4.5.7 does not have.
Blocking repo-server egress does not prevent this, because a `file://` remote never leaves the pod. Restricting Application `get`, or blocking `POST /api/v1/applications/manifestsWithFiles`, closes only the upload path. A Kustomization committed to Git is still built on the next sync.
There is no complete workaround besides upgrading.
### Credits
The Argo CD team would like to thank @hoang-prod and @yabeow for responsibly disclosing this issue according to our [security reporting guidelines](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/blob/master/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability).
### References
* Introducing commit: [25badeb7a1e154805340bb7237e0ce671f3772dd](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/commit/25badeb7a1e154805340bb7237e0ce671f3772dd) ([#12299](https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/pull/12299)), first released in v2.7.0 * [Custom Kustomize versions](https://argo-cd.readthedocs.io/en/stable/user-guide/kustomize/#custom-kustomize-versions)

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Knowledge base reordering, publishing and administration possible without the required permission
item.description:
CVSS 7.2 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:N/VI:H/VA:H/SC:L/SI:L/SA:N) · CWE-269, CWE-862, CWE-863
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Agents with read-only knowledge base access were able to change the order of knowledge base categories and answers, and to change the publication state of answers. Both are intended to be restricted to knowledge base editors, but the permission checks accepted any level of knowledge base access. Because agents receive read access by default, any agent could publish answers to the public help site, archive or un-archive them, and set the publication dates. Answers meant to stay internal could therefore be made available to anonymous visitors, and published answers could be removed from the site.
Separately, agents with knowledge base editor access were able to create, change and delete knowledge bases themselves, although this is reserved for knowledge base administrators. An editor could change the public address and the appearance of a knowledge base, take it offline, or delete it together with all of its categories and answers.

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Customer-visible ticket update responses leak unredacted user and organization data
item.description:
CVSS 7.1 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-359, CWE-863
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Ticket update responses could include unredacted personal data that should have been hidden from the requesting user.
When a customer updated one of their own tickets and requested a detailed response, the reply could contain unfiltered details about the agents involved in that ticket - such as private phone numbers, postal address, department and internal notes - as well as internal information about their organization, including internal notes and the VIP flag. The same data is correctly hidden when simply viewing the ticket; only the update responses were affected.
Customers could therefore obtain personal information about support staff and internal administrative notes that are meant for internal use only.

item.title: [LOW] zammad/zammad — Clipboard HTML injection via unescaped user and organization display name
item.description:
CVSS 2.1 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:N/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-116
Affected: - other/Zammad >= 7.0.0, <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
The desktop view offers a button to copy a user's or an organization's name together with a link to their profile. The copied content was assembled without properly escaping the name, so a name that contains markup was copied as markup rather than as plain text.
An attacker could use this by choosing a crafted name — for example by sending an email into the helpdesk with a specially prepared sender name, which does not require an account. If an agent then copies that name and pastes it into a formatted text field, such as a reply to a customer, the pasted content can contain a link or other elements chosen by the attacker instead of the intended profile link. This can be used to make a message written by an agent point recipients at an attacker-controlled destination.

item.title: [MEDIUM] zammad/zammad — Channel administration APIs return stored channel credentials in clear text
item.description:
CVSS 6.9 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:H/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-116, CWE-200, CWE-522
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad stores the access data of the configured channels, such as Facebook page access tokens, the Telegram bot token, the SMS gateway token and the passwords or OAuth tokens of email accounts. Whenever a channel configuration is sent to the browser, these values are supposed to be replaced by a masked placeholder, so that stored access data cannot be read back once it has been saved. For several channels this masking did not take effect.
As a result, an administrator holding the permission for one of the affected channels could obtain the stored access data in clear text through the channel administration APIs, and use it to access the connected external service directly, outside of Zammad. Affected are the Facebook, Telegram, SMS and email channels, including the Google and Microsoft 365 variants.
Only instances that have such a channel configured are affected, and only administrators who already hold the administration permission for that channel type could read the access data.

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Missing authorization on ticket articles can expose article content to unauthorized users
item.description:
CVSS 7.1 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-639
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
A missing authorization check in the ticket-article creation endpoint allows any authenticated customer to read the content of arbitrary ticket articles, including internal agent notes and articles belonging to other organizations, that they are not permitted to view. This constitutes a confidentiality break of Zammad's core ticketing data, requiring no elevated privileges and no user interaction.

item.title: [MEDIUM] zammad/zammad — Stored HTML injection in Knowledge Base video widget rendered inside Zammad enables forced session switching
item.description:
CVSS 6.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:P/VC:N/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:N) · CWE-79, CWE-352, CWE-838
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
A user with Knowledge Base editing rights for a category can embed a video widget in an answer with a specially crafted value. When that answer is opened in Zammad's knowledge base view, the value is inserted into the page's HTML without being escaped for the context it appears in, allowing it to break out and inject additional HTML into the page. The answer does not need to be published for this to happen.
When another user who has permission to switch between user sessions opens the affected answer, the injected HTML causes their browser to silently send a request to Zammad's session-switching endpoint using their own active credentials. This results in switching their session to an account chosen by the person who wrote the Knowledge Base answer. No action is required from the viewer beyond opening the answer.

item.title: [MEDIUM] zammad/zammad — Unscoped GraphQL template query and subscription bypass TemplatePolicy scope
item.description:
CVSS 5.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-862
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Ticket templates were not restricted to the users allowed to see them. Agents were able to see templates that had been deactivated, and customers were able to receive the contents of all templates — including deactivated ones — whenever any template was created, changed or deleted.
The disclosed information covered the name of each template and the values it fills in, such as prepared ticket titles, message texts, and the customer, group, owner or tag settings stored in it. Access was limited to reading; it was not possible to change templates, tickets or any other data this way. How sensitive the disclosed information was depended on what each installation had stored in its templates.

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Second-order SQL injection in ticket overview sorting
item.description:
CVSS 7.2 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:H/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H) · CWE-89, CWE-94
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad's ticket overview handling contained a second-order SQL injection flaw. A user permitted to create or modify ticket overviews could store a crafted value in an overview's sort-order configuration. That value was not restricted to the expected sort keywords, and when tickets for the overview were later retrieved through the API, it was incorporated into the underlying database query without being safely escaped for that context. Triggering it required no action by any other user.
An attacker able to reach this could have read arbitrary data from the Zammad database — including other users' password hashes, ticket content and configuration data — regardless of what their own role was meant to grant them access to. The further reachable impact depended on the privileges of the database account the installation runs Zammad with. Installations using the packaged (Linux) setup, where Zammad runs with a restricted non-superuser database role, were limited to that read impact; where the database role held elevated privileges, the same access could have been extended to reading and writing files on the database host and, from there, to executing arbitrary code with the privileges of the database server process.
Reported by: Gabriele PARIS from NATO Cyber Security Centre (NCSC)

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Arbitrary configuration disclosure via recent view endpoint
item.description:
CVSS 8.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:H/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-639, CWE-862
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Any authenticated user, including the lowest-privileged customer role, could read the name and stored value of arbitrary application configuration settings. Because the configuration also holds deployment secrets, this included credentials a non-administrative user would otherwise never reach, such as the Elasticsearch endpoint password and the credentials of configured import sources.
Affected were all settings neither marked as protected nor restricted to a specific permission — roughly a quarter of all settings on a default installation, including the credential-bearing ones. Sensitive values existed only where the corresponding feature was configured. Access was read-only and limited to configuration data.
Upgrading does not undo an exposure that already happened. Administrators should rotate the affected credentials after upgrading.
Reported by: Gabriele PARIS from NATO Cyber Security Centre (NCSC)

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Stored XSS in ticket zoom via attacker-controlled article preferences
item.description:
CVSS 8.5 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-79, CWE-915
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
A customer was able to store content of their own choosing in the internal metadata of a ticket article they created. When an agent later opened that ticket, parts of this metadata were displayed without being neutralized for safe rendering, so the stored content was interpreted as active content in the agent's browser session.
As a result, a user with only standard customer permissions was able to cause code to run in the session of any agent who opened the affected ticket, without any special configuration or elevated privileges. Because the code ran with the agent's session, its impact extended to whatever that agent could reach, including tickets in other groups and internal notes.

item.title: [CRITICAL] zammad/zammad — Unfiltered sign-up and ticket update fields allow cross-organization ticket disclosure and takeover
item.description:
CVSS 9.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-287, CWE-863, CWE-915
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad's public sign-up form accepted account fields that it should have ignored. An attacker without any account could use this to register on an email address they did not own, have that account treated as already email-confirmed, and add it to any organization in the system.
Because members of an organization can see each other's tickets by default, such an account could then read and reply to tickets of other customers of those organizations. A second issue allowed any customer account to change fields of another customer's ticket in the same organization — including which customer the ticket belongs to — which could take a ticket away from the person who opened it.

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Remote code execution via template sanitizer bypass in automation configuration
item.description:
CVSS 8.6 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:H/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-20, CWE-94, CWE-1336
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
A user allowed to configure automations in Zammad — such as triggers, scheduled jobs, ticket macros or AI agents — could execute arbitrary commands on the server hosting Zammad. A specially crafted value in an automation's configuration bypassed the escaping Zammad applied to such text, and the resulting code ran with the privileges of the Zammad application process. No interaction from another user was required.
This could have been used to read or modify any data reachable by that process, including the ticket and customer database and any credentials available to it. On a default installation the required permission is held only by full administrators, who already have supported ways of running code on the server, so the practical gain there was limited; it became a genuine privilege escalation where a scoped or delegated role, or a hosted deployment, granted automation configuration without full administrative access. Installations with AI agents configured were exposed on an additional path, because values returned by the configured AI provider were processed in the same way.

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Inactive sessions remain authorized over ActionCable GraphQL
item.description:
CVSS 7.1 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-613
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
An account that had been deactivated in Zammad could retain access to ticket data through Zammad's real-time WebSocket connections. The web-based HTTP interface correctly rejected such accounts after deactivation, but the WebSocket connections restored the session's user without applying the same check for whether the account was still active.
As a result, a deactivated agent could continue to read tickets within the scope of their previous group and role assignments, and a deactivated customer could continue to read their own ticket history and shared-organization data, until the underlying session expired or was removed. Because these connections also carry Zammad's live updates, the exposure was not limited to data that already existed at the point of deactivation: ticket changes and notifications occurring afterwards could continue to reach the affected account. The issue required an existing, retained session for an account that was later deactivated; it did not allow a new account, or an attacker without a valid session, to gain access.
Administrators who deactivated accounts while running an affected version should treat any sessions still stored for those accounts as potentially usable and remove them in addition to upgrading. Installations in which no account was ever deactivated were not exposed.

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Session identifier disclosed in authenticated configuration response enabled off-host session takeover
item.description:
CVSS 7.4 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-522, CWE-807
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad returned the signed-in user's session identifier in an authenticated configuration response, where scripts running in that user's browser were able to read it — which the session cookie's `HttpOnly` flag is meant to prevent. The real-time channel of the classic web interface also accepted such an identifier as proof of identity.
An attacker who had already gained script execution in a user's session, through a separate weakness, could copy the identifier to a machine of their own and act as that user from there for the life of the session, without their password or second factor. This included reading everything the account could see, such as tickets with their internal notes, and creating or changing data in the user's name. The reach scaled with the privileges of the affected account.

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Deactivated roles still granted knowledge base editor access
item.description:
CVSS 7.6 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-266, CWE-863
Affected: - other/Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad did not check whether a role was still active when resolving the knowledge base access that role granted. A user who still held a role an administrator had set to inactive therefore kept editor access: they could read internal categories and answers that are not published on the public help site, and create, modify and permanently delete them.
The impact was limited to knowledge base content; no ticket data, user records or credentials were exposed. Only installations that deactivated a role carrying knowledge base permissions while it was still assigned to users were affected; administrators who withdrew access that way should review those users' knowledge base activity.

item.title: [MEDIUM] zammad/zammad — Deactivated roles still granted ticket group access in overviews and search
item.description:
CVSS 6.0 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-266, CWE-863
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Deactivating a role in Zammad did not revoke the group access it granted. An agent who still held such a deactivated role, and who could still sign in through another active role with agent permissions, retained access to everything scoped by those groups: tickets stayed listed in overviews, search and ticket selection, exposing metadata such as title, number, customer, state and owner, and group-restricted text modules, macros and shared ticket drafts remained available as well.
Opening an affected ticket was correctly refused, so ticket article content stayed protected and no ticket could be changed. Only installations that revoked access by deactivating a role while leaving it assigned to users were affected; administrators who did so should assume the affected agents retained that access throughout.

item.title: [MEDIUM] zammad/zammad — Disclosure of names of users from other organizations to customers
item.description:
CVSS 5.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-201, CWE-359, CWE-863
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Users can be assigned to further organizations in addition to their primary one. Customers are only meant to see the name and active state of their own organization, but due to a missing check on one attribute, a customer reading their own organization also received the list of users assigned to it as secondary members, along with the names of those users.
As a result, a customer could learn the names of users who belong to other organizations. Only names, the active state and avatar information were exposed, no contact details, notes or ticket content, and nothing could be modified this way. Only instances that use secondary organization assignments are affected.

item.title: [MEDIUM] zammad/zammad — Ticket data of no-longer-accessible tickets disclosed to agents via online notification API
item.description:
CVSS 5.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-359, CWE-639, CWE-863
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Agents who had received an in-app notification about a ticket kept read access to it after losing access — because the ticket moved to a group they cannot see, or their group permissions were narrowed. Opening the ticket was correctly refused, but the notification could still be fetched individually through the API, and its response carried the ticket's title, number, state, priority, escalation data, owner and customer assignment, plus the linked users' names and email addresses.
Only a valid agent account and an existing notification were required, with no action by anyone else. Exposure was limited to tickets the agent still held a notification for, and notifications are retained only for a limited period; other users' notifications were not reachable. Responses carried current data, so later changes were disclosed too. Only installations using group-based access to separate agents from tickets were affected.

item.title: [MEDIUM] zammad/zammad — Ticket link list disclosed the existence and relation of tickets outside the user's permission scope
item.description:
CVSS 5.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-862, CWE-863
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
The REST endpoint listing an object's links required a session, but never checked whether the requesting user was allowed to see the object they asked about. Any authenticated user, including a customer without agent permissions, could therefore learn that a ticket outside their permission scope existed and was linked to one of their own tickets, and of what link type. As ticket ids are sequential, this could be repeated to find every such link.
No content of the inaccessible ticket was exposed: title, number, customer, group and articles stayed protected, and only links to objects the requester could already read were revealed. Installations that never link tickets across permission boundaries were unaffected, as was the GraphQL API.

item.title: [MEDIUM] zammad/zammad — Group configuration and email address disclosure to authenticated users via getting started endpoint
item.description:
CVSS 5.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-863
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
An API endpoint that supplies start-up information to the web interface required a valid login, but did not check what the account was permitted to see. Any authenticated user, including a customer without agent or administrator permissions, could read the configuration of all active groups — internal group notes, signature and sender-address assignments, and internal ticket handling settings — together with the full list of configured email addresses. Groups the account had no relationship to were included as well.
The exposure was read-only. No ticket content and no personal data of users or customers were affected. Installations that allow customer self-registration, or that keep internal remarks in group notes, are most affected.

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Activity stream disclosed content of tickets moved out of an agent's groups
item.description:
CVSS 7.1 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-863
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad's activity stream returned information about tickets that the requesting agent was no longer allowed to open. Once a ticket had been moved into a group the agent has no access to, or the agent's access to its group had been withdrawn, activity entries recorded earlier remained visible to that agent. Depending on which representation of the activity stream was requested, those entries disclosed the ticket's title, number, current group and customer, and the subject and body of its articles, although the ticket itself was correctly refused. Only agents who previously had access to the affected ticket were able to see this; customers were not affected, and no data could be changed this way.

item.title: [MEDIUM] zammad/zammad — Password reset endpoint disclosed whether an account existed via response timing
item.description:
CVSS 6.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-203, CWE-208
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad's password reset function answered every request identically, so that it would not reveal whether an account exists for the submitted email address or login. The time the request took differed, however, depending on whether an account was found, because further processing was only performed in that case. An unauthenticated user able to reach the login screen could therefore determine whether a given address belonged to an active Zammad account.
Only that fact was exposed. No personal data, ticket content or other account information could be read, and nothing could be modified. The password reset function had to be enabled and outgoing email had to be configured for the difference to be observable. Existing rate limits — three requests per minute per source IP address and per submitted address — restricted how many addresses could be checked. Both the classic and the new interface were affected.
Reported by: Gabriele PARIS from NATO Cyber Security Centre (NCSC)

item.title: [LOW] zammad/zammad — Group collection push disclosed full group records to any authenticated session
item.description:
CVSS 2.3 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:L/UI:N/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-285
Affected: - Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad pushed complete group records to every connected browser session over the WebSocket collection update, without applying the field scope that limits group data for non-agent users. Any authenticated user, including a customer with no agent permissions, received all attributes of every group in the system whenever a group was created, changed or deleted.
The disclosed data included internal administrative notes, group configuration such as assignment timeouts and shared-draft and signature settings, the list of member user IDs of each group, and groups that were inactive or that the user had no relationship to. No ticket content and no personal contact data were exposed, and the push was read-only, so no group could be altered this way.

item.title: [MEDIUM] zammad/zammad — Stored XSS in desktop tree select fields via whitespace-only filter
item.description:
CVSS 4.8 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:A/VC:L/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-79, CWE-116
Affected: - other/Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad's new desktop interface rendered option labels in tree select fields as HTML instead of plain text when the dropdown filter contained only whitespace, which happens routinely while typing or deleting a search term. A label containing specially crafted markup was then parsed by the browser instead of being displayed literally.
Tree select labels come from object attribute options, group names and knowledge base category titles. A user with permission to maintain any of these, for example a knowledge base editor or an administrator limited to object management, could have stored such a label. Script embedded in it could have executed in the session of any other agent or administrator who opened the affected field and filtered it, allowing actions and data access with the victim's permissions.
Only the desktop interface was affected; the legacy interface and the mobile interface were not.

item.title: [CRITICAL] zammad/zammad — Multi-factor authentication could be bypassed through the email verification flow
item.description:
CVSS 9.1 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-287, CWE-304, CWE-308
Affected: - other/Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad's email verification flow established a fully authenticated session for an existing user account without requiring the second factor configured for that account. Multi-factor authentication was enforced during a normal sign-in, but not on this path.
An account was affected if it had never completed email verification — the default state for accounts created by an administrator, through the API, a directory import, or an incoming email — and had multi-factor authentication configured. Exploitation required possession of the verification email sent to the account's own address; knowing the address was not sufficient, and no password was needed. The resulting session carried the full permissions of the account, up to administrator, and could be used to create a personal access token that outlived it.
Installations relying on multi-factor authentication for agent or administrator accounts are affected most.

item.title: [HIGH] zammad/zammad — Stored XSS in desktop autocomplete fields via unescaped option label
item.description:
CVSS 8.6 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-79, CWE-116
Affected: - other/Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
Zammad's desktop interface rendered an autocomplete option label as HTML whenever the label did not contain the text the agent had typed. Only labels matching that text were escaped, and a server-side search regularly returns records whose label does not contain it — a user found by email address, shown by name — so unescaped labels reached the browser during ordinary work.
Those labels came from user and organization names, which anyone able to register an account could set. Crafted markup in a name was therefore parsed by the browser and executed in the session of the agent who looked the record up, with that agent's permissions.
The legacy interface and the mobile interface were not affected.

item.title: [LOW] zammad/zammad — Forward quote header discloses agent email addresses
item.description:
CVSS 2.1 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-359
Affected: - other/Zammad <= 7.2.0 (patched: 7.2.1)
---
When an agent forwarded an existing message from a ticket, the quoted message header that Zammad generated could contain the personal email address of the agent who wrote the original message, instead of the shared email address of the group.
As a result, that agent's personal address could be sent to the external recipient of the forwarded message. Because the forwarded message is stored as a publicly visible article, the address was also readable by the customer of the ticket, even though customers are otherwise never given the email addresses of agents.
Only instances whose sender format for outgoing email is configured to show the agent name alone are affected. Instances using the default sender format are not affected.

item.title: [MEDIUM] espocrm/espocrm — IDOR allowing users with access to Import scope to extract data from attachments with known ID
item.description:
CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N) · CWE-639, CWE-862
Affected: - espocrm/espocrm <= 10.0.6 (patched: 10.0.7)
---
## Summary
I identified an authenticated authorization bypass in EspoCRM’s import workflow.
`POST /api/v1/Import` accepts a caller-controlled `attachmentId`, but the backend does not verify that the current user is authorized to read that attachment before opening it from storage.
An attacker can create their own Import record using another user’s attachment ID. After the Import record is created, the attacker can call the error export endpoint on their own Import record. EspoCRM then re-opens the original source attachment and copies source rows from that file into a new downloadable CSV attachment owned by the attacker.
This allows a low-privileged authenticated user to disclose contents of another user’s attachment when the attachment ID is known.

item.title: [MEDIUM] espocrm/espocrm — Note read does not run ACL output filter against audit data exposing values of fields that are restricted with field-level security
item.description:
CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N) · CWE-200, CWE-863
